rationale: Both candidates correctly surface and resolve the ground truth's sole substantive concern (the now-removed trust_remote_code kwarg / stale PR body), and both flag the untested cache path and the unrelated NPU CI failure with proper hedging. X pads its report with ~5 near-duplicate restatements of the same trust_remote_code point under a heavy evidence-quote format, which is well-grounded but adds bulk without new insight. Y is more concise and surfaces two genuinely novel, high-value findings beyond the ground truth (the except-Exception fallback now stickily caching a degraded kernel process-wide, and the third version=None fallback becoming dead code on kernels>=0.15), each with concrete actionable fixes, giving it slightly better precision and actionability despite a couple of unverified 'I ran/verified' claims.
